questions.question_text: Define the Goldilocks Zone and its significance for habitability.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The Goldilocks Zone is the orbital region around a star where temperatures are 'neither too hot nor too cold', allowing water to remain liquid on planetary surfaces.

questions.question_text: Explain why Venus is inhospitable despite being similar in size to Earth.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Venus orbits too close to the Sun and possesses an extremely dense CO2 atmosphere driving runaway greenhouse effects, raising surface temperatures to 460 deg C and boiling away all water.
